name: Lakeridge Highway
summary: Travelers on Lakeridge Highway face ruin and danger along Lake Everstill's southern shore. Before the First War, this vital, heavily traveled road carried trade through Redridge; now gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage perilous.

sections.title: A Fallen Artery
sections.body: Before the First War, Lakeridge Highway carried goods and travelers through Redridge as a busy trade route along Lake Everstill's southern shore. In those peaceful days, travelers crossed between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under Stormwind's protection. The Horde's march shattered that safety, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate.

sections.title: Peril on the Road
sections.body: After Blackrock orcs seized Stonewatch Keep, regular road repairs and patrols stopped. Lakeridge Highway soon crumbled into an overgrown track, contested by savage gnoll packs. Stormwind's forces are spread thin and cannot reinforce Lakeshire, leaving the highway officially unsafe. Travelers bound for the eastern ridges must face gnoll ambushes along the way.

faq.q: Where does the Lakeridge Highway lead?
faq.answer: Lakeridge Highway follows Lake Everstill's southern shore east from Lakeshire toward the foothills around Stonewatch Keep and the eastern mountains of Redridge.

Lakeridge Highway fell into disuse after the First War, especially when Blackrock orcs fortified Stonewatch Keep. Stormwind lacked the forces to secure and maintain the road, leaving hostile gnolls free to move in and choking off civilian travel.

faq.q: What threats wander the road today?
faq.answer: Aggressive gnolls ambush travelers who stray from Lakeshire, while Blackrock orc scouts still operate from the eastern strongholds.
No. Before the First War, Lakeridge Highway was a well-kept, heavily traveled route that safely linked Redridge's heartland with its eastern outposts.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Lakeridge Highway shows how far Stormwind's neglected frontier reaches: roads just beyond Lakeshire have been left to gnolls and orcs for lack of reinforcements.
